D. Whitfield, on 05/08, stating "we are looking into it." Client asked if he
should respond. Advised client to acknowledge receipt but not to discuss the
legal claim. Client said he would reply "OK, thanks."

05/15/2024 – R. Castellanos.
Received certified mail return receipt. Letter signed by "D. Whitfield" on

05/21/2024 – K. Okafor.
Client called. He reported that on 05/19, he received a notice from the
landlord stating his lease would not be renewed at the end of the current
term (lease expires 07/31/2024). Notice states reason: "non-renewal, no
cause." Client is concerned this is retaliation for the demand letter.
Advise client to keep the notice. We will review the lease terms and Oregon
law regarding non-renewal notice requirements. ORS 90.427 requires 90 days'
notice for a no-cause non-renewal if the tenancy has lasted one year or more.
Client has been in the unit since 06/2021. The notice is dated 05/19/2024,
which is only 73 days before lease end. This appears to be insufficient
notice. Will draft a response.

Case File 2024-2210 status is closed. Record status: historical.

----------------------------------------------------------------------

05/23/2024 – R. Castellanos.
Drafted response to the non-renewal notice. Letter to Alder Property Group,
LLC, dated 05/23/2024, asserting that the notice is defective due to
insufficient notice period per ORS 90.427, and that the non-renewal appears
retaliatory in violation of ORS 90.385. Demanded withdrawal of the notice.
Sent via certified mail, return receipt requested. Tracking #9405 5116 9930
0453 8722 03.

----------------------------------------------------------------------

05/30/2024 – K. Okafor.
No response from landlord to the 05/23 letter as of today. Client called to
check status. Advised him to wait. Also noted that the ceiling leak has gotten
worse; client sent photos via email (attached to case file in digital folder,
subfolder "Photos_2024-05-30"). Photos show water stains on the living room
ceiling and a new drip in the hallway.

----------------------------------------------------------------------

06/04/2024 – R. Castellanos.

"D. Whitfield" on 05/28/2024. Still no substantive response.

Case File 2024-2210 – Closed

06/10/2024 – K. Okafor.
Client called. He received a voicemail from Alder Property Group on 06/07
stating they would “review the matter” but no written response. Client is
anxious. Explained that the 90-day notice period runs from the date the
tenant is served, and that even if the landlord withdraws the notice, we
should get it in writing. Client agreed to wait until 06/21 before
escalating.

Also, client reported the hallway drip has started staining the carpet.
Advised him to document with photos and to keep all receipts for any
cleaning supplies. Referred him to the City of Portland rental housing
inspections program if the landlord does not address the leak within 14
days. Client said he would call them himself if needed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

06/17/2024 – R. Castellanos.
Received letter from Alder Property Group, LLC, dated 06/12/2024. They
withdraw the non-renewal notice. They state the lease will be renewed on a
month-to-month basis after 07/31/2024, per the original lease terms. They
do not admit any defect in the original notice. They also state they will
send a maintenance contractor to inspect the ceiling leak on 06/20/2024
between 1:00 PM and 4:00 PM.

Reviewed lease. Section 3 of the lease states that after the initial term,
the tenancy converts to month-to-month unless either party gives written
notice of non-renewal at least 90 days prior to the end of the term. The
landlord’s position is consistent with the lease. The withdrawal of the
non-renewal notice resolves the retaliation issue for now, but we should
monitor for any further adverse action within six months.

Sent copy of the letter to client via email and regular mail. Advised him
to allow the contractor access but to document the condition of the ceiling
and hallway before and after the inspection.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

06/20/2024 – K. Okafor.
Client called at 3:10 PM. Contractor (name: “Mike” from Alder’s vendor,
Pacific Crest Maintenance) arrived at 1:30 PM and left at 2:45 PM. Client
says Mike looked at the living room ceiling, took photos, and said he would
“report back.” Mike did not do any repair work. Client asked if he should
expect a follow-up. I told him to wait a week and then call the landlord’s
office to ask for a written repair timeline.

Client also mentioned that he received a text from the landlord’s office
on 06/19 asking if he would be interested in signing a new one-year lease
at a rent increase of $75/month. Client is worried this is retaliation
after the withdrawal of the non-renewal notice. I told him not to respond
to the text until we review it. He will forward the text to me.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

06/24/2024 – R. Castellanos.
Reviewed the text message forwarded by client. Sent 06/19/2024 from a
number registered to Alder Property Group. The text offers a one-year
renewal at $1,475/month (current rent is $1,400/month). The offer is not
in writing and does not state an expiration date.

Per ORS 90.385, a landlord may not retaliate by increasing rent within 180
days of a tenant complaint. The demand letter regarding the mold was sent
in April 2024, which is within the 180-day window. The non-renewal notice
was issued 05/19/2024, also within the window. This rent increase offer,
coming after the withdrawal of the non-renewal, could be viewed as
retaliatory. However, proving retaliation for a rent increase is harder
than for a non-renewal because the landlord can claim market adjustment.

documents.content:

She said she has not yet received a decision on her rental assistance application. I advised her to contact the rental assistance program directly for a status update and to keep the notice and any proof of application. I also suggested she speak with the landlord about a possible extension. – R. Chen

7/24/2024 – Client left a message asking whether she should appear at a court hearing. She stated she received a summons for an eviction case, case number 2024-3341, filed by Meridian Heights Apartments. I retrieved the case from the court's online docket. A hearing is scheduled for 8/5/2024 at 9:00 a.m. before Judge M. Alvarez. I returned her call and advised her to attend the hearing and to bring all documents related to her rent payments and rental assistance application. I told her we would review the summons and complaint if she brings them to the office. – R. Chen

7/29/2024 – Ms. Santos came to the office with the summons and complaint for case 2024-3341. The complaint alleges nonpayment of rent for July 2024 in the amount of $1,050, plus a $75 late fee, and seeks possession of the premises. I reviewed the documents and noted the filing date of 7/23/2024. I advised her that she must file an answer by 8/2/2024 to avoid a default judgment. She asked if we could represent her. I explained that we would need to determine eligibility and that I would consult with Atty. Okafor. I took copies of the summons, complaint, and her bank statements showing the June payment. – R. Chen

8/1/2024 – Reviewed case 2024-3341 with Atty. Okafor. He agreed that Ms. Santos may have a defense based on her timely June payment and the landlord's failure to credit it. He authorized limited representation for the purpose of filing an answer and appearing at the 8/5/2024 hearing. I prepared the answer, asserting the affirmative defense of payment and requesting dismissal. Ms. Santos signed the answer at the office. I filed it electronically with the court and served a copy on the landlord's attorney, D. Whitfield, by email. – R. Chen

Case File 2024-1187 status is open. Record status: current.

8/5/2024 – Attended hearing in case 2024-3341 with Atty. Okafor. The landlord's attorney, D. Whitfield, stated that the landlord had applied the June payment to the June rent and that the July rent remains unpaid. Atty. Okafor argued that the landlord failed to provide a credit toward the prior late fee balance and that the client's rental assistance application was still pending. The court continued the matter to 8/19/2024 to allow the parties to attempt resolution. The judge ordered the parties to exchange documents related to the payment history by 8/12/2024. – R. Chen

8/8/2024 – Sent email to D. Whitfield requesting a copy of the tenant ledger for Ms. Santos's account from January 2024 to present. Also requested confirmation of whether the rental assistance payment for May rent was applied and whether any credits were issued. – R. Chen

8/12/2024 – Received email from D. Whitfield attaching the tenant ledger. The ledger shows a balance of $1,125 as of 8/1/2024, with no credits applied after the May rental assistance payment. I reviewed the ledger against Ms. Santos's bank statements and noted a discrepancy: the ledger does not reflect the June 3, 2024 payment of $1,050. I called Ms. Santos to confirm the payment was made by debit card from her checking account. She confirmed. I prepared a summary of the discrepancy and sent it to Atty. Okafor for review. – R. Chen

documents.title: Case File 2024-1187 – Maria Santos
documents.content:
8/15/2024 – Ms. Santos dropped off the rental assistance approval letter dated 8/13/2024. The letter states that assistance of $850 per month will be paid directly to the landlord beginning with the September rent. I made a copy and placed the original in the client file. I sent the copy to D. Whitfield with a note that the September rent will be covered by the housing authority. – R. Chen

8/16/2024 – Prepared the supplemental brief regarding the June 3, 2024 payment. Atty. Okafor reviewed and approved it. Filed the brief with the court and served on D. Whitfield by email. I also called Ms. Santos to confirm she would attend the 8/19/2024 hearing. She confirmed. – R. Chen

8/19/2024 – Attended hearing in case 2024-3341 with Atty. Okafor. The landlord's attorney, D. Whitfield, acknowledged receipt of the rental assistance approval letter. The court asked both parties whether they had exchanged the payment history documents as ordered. We confirmed that we had received the tenant ledger from the landlord, and we had provided the supplemental brief and the rental assistance letter. Atty. Okafor argued that the ledger is incomplete because it does not reflect the June 3, 2024 payment. D. Whitfield stated that the landlord's records show the June payment was applied to the June rent, and the balance of $1,125 represents the July rent and late fees. The court reviewed the documents and continued the matter to 9/15/2024 for an evidentiary hearing. The judge ordered the landlord to produce the complete payment history, including any internal notes regarding the June 3, 2024 payment, by 9/3/2024. – R. Chen

8/20/2024 – Sent email to D. Whitfield requesting the landlord's internal notes regarding the June 3, 2024 payment, as ordered by the court. Also requested a copy of the landlord's bank statement showing the deposit of the June payment, if available. – R. Chen

Case File 2024-1187 hearing_date is 2024-09-15. Record status: current.

8/22/2024 – Received email from D. Whitfield stating that the landlord does not have a bank statement showing the June 3, 2024 payment because the payment was made by debit card and the landlord's records only show the card transaction. He attached a copy of the transaction receipt from the landlord's point-of-sale system showing a payment of $1,050 on 6/3/2024. I reviewed the receipt and noted that it shows the payment was applied to the June rent. I called Ms. Santos to confirm that the debit card used matches her checking account. She confirmed. I prepared a summary of the receipt and sent it to Atty. Okafor. – R. Chen

8/26/2024 – Reviewed the point-of-sale receipt with Atty. Okafor. He noted that the receipt does not show how the payment was applied to the account, only that it was received. He instructed me to prepare a trial exhibit list for the 9/15/2024 hearing, including the tenant ledger, the point-of-sale receipt, Ms. Santos's bank statement showing the debit card charge, and the rental assistance approval letter. I prepared the exhibit list and sent it to D. Whitfield for review. – R. Chen

8/28/2024 – Received email from D. Whitfield with no objections to the exhibit list. He stated that the landlord will produce the complete payment history by 9/3/2024 as ordered. I called Ms. Santos to confirm that she has no additional documents to provide. She said she does not. – R. Chen

9/3/2024 – Received the complete payment history from D. Whitfield. The history includes a line item for the June 3, 2024 payment of $1,050, applied to the June rent, and a line item for the July rent of $1,050, unpaid. The balance as of 9/1/2024 is $1,125, which includes the July rent and a late fee of $75. I reviewed the history against the earlier ledger and noted that the earlier ledger omitted the June 3, 2024 payment. I prepared a comparison summary and sent it to Atty. Okafor. – R. Chen

documents.title: Case File 2024-1187 – Maria Santos
documents.content:
**Case File 2024-1187 – Maria Santos**

**9/4/2024** – Received email from D. Whitfield stating that the landlord will not provide the original lease agreement from 2021 because the property management company that signed the lease went out of business and the current landlord only has a scanned copy. He attached the scanned copy. I reviewed it and noted that the signatures are legible and the rent amount matches the current ledger. I called Ms. Santos to confirm that she signed this lease. She said she did, in April 2021. I prepared a note summarizing the scan and sent it to Atty. Okafor. – R. Chen

**9/5/2024** – Prepared the trial notebook for the 9/15/2024 hearing. Included the exhibit list, the tenant ledger, the point-of-sale receipt, Ms. Santos's bank statement, the rental assistance approval letter, the complete payment history from D. Whitfield, and the scanned lease. I also included a copy of the court's standing order on summary process proceedings. Sent the notebook to Atty. Okafor for review. – R. Chen

**9/6/2024** – Atty. Okafor returned the trial notebook with notes. He asked me to prepare a proposed stipulation of facts for the landlord's counsel to review, covering the following: (1) the lease was signed in April 2021; (2) the rent is $1,050 per month; (3) the June 3, 2024 payment of $1,050 was made and applied to the June rent; (4) the July rent is unpaid; (5) the balance as of 9/1/2024 is $1,125. I drafted the stipulation and sent it to D. Whitfield. – R. Chen

**9/9/2024** – Received email from D. Whitfield declining to sign the proposed stipulation. He stated that the landlord disputes only the application of the June 3, 2024 payment, arguing that the payment was applied to the May rent, which was also unpaid. He noted that the tenant ledger from the property management company shows the May rent as unpaid. I reviewed the ledger and confirmed that it does not show any payment for May or June. I called Ms. Santos to ask if she has any record of a May rent payment. She said she does not, and that she believed the May rent was paid by the rental assistance program. I checked the rental assistance approval letter and noted that it covers rent for May and June 2024, but the letter does not show proof of disbursement. I prepared a summary of this discrepancy and sent it to Atty. Okafor. – R. Chen

**9/10/2024** – Atty. Okafor instructed me to contact the rental assistance program to request proof of disbursement for May and June 2024. I called the program and spoke with a representative named L. Morales. She confirmed that the program issued a payment to the landlord for the May 2024 rent on 5/15/2024 in the amount of $1,050, and a payment for the June 2024 rent on 6/3/2024 in the amount of $1,050. She said she would email me the payment records. I received the email later that day with two payment confirmations. I reviewed them and noted that the June 3, 2024 payment confirmation shows the same transaction as the point-of-sale receipt from D. Whitfield. I prepared a summary and sent it to Atty. Okafor. – R. Chen

**9/11/2024** – Received email from D. Whitfield stating that the landlord will produce an amended ledger showing the May 2024 rent as paid, but will continue to dispute the application of the June 3, 2024 payment. He stated that the landlord's position is that the June 3, 2024 payment was applied to the May rent, not the June rent, and that the June rent remains unpaid. I called Ms. Santos to inform her of the landlord's position. She said she does not understand why the landlord is disputing this, and asked if she needs to attend the hearing. I told her that Atty. Okafor will advise her, but that it would be helpful for her to be present. She said she will attend. – R. Chen

documents.title: Case File 2024-1187 – Maria Santos
documents.content:
**Case File 2024-1187 – Maria Santos**
**Community Legal Aid of Meridian**

---

**9/12/2024** – Atty. Okafor reviewed the payment confirmations from the rental assistance program and the amended ledger statement from D. Whitfield. He instructed me to draft a response to the landlord's position, arguing that the June 3, 2024 payment was clearly designated for the June rent based on the payment confirmation from the rental assistance program, which lists the June rent period. I drafted the response and sent it to Atty. Okafor for review. – R. Chen

**9/13/2024** – Atty. Okafor approved the response. I sent it to D. Whitfield via email and fax. The response includes a copy of the June 3, 2024 payment confirmation and the rental assistance approval letter. I also called Ms. Santos to confirm she received the hearing notice for the eviction case. She confirmed she received it and will be present at the hearing on 9/17/2024 at 9:00 AM at the Meridian County Courthouse, Room 204. – R. Chen

**9/16/2024** – Received email from D. Whitfield stating that the landlord will not withdraw the eviction action and will proceed with the hearing. He stated that the landlord maintains the position that the June 3, 2024 payment was applied to the May rent and that the June rent remains unpaid. I called Ms. Santos to inform her of this and to confirm her attendance at the hearing tomorrow. She confirmed she will be there. I prepared a hearing file with all relevant documents, including the rental assistance approval letter, the payment confirmations, the amended ledger, and our response. – R. Chen

**9/17/2024** – Attended the eviction hearing with Ms. Santos. Atty. Okafor represented her. The judge reviewed the documents and asked the landlord's representative, D. Whitfield, to explain why the June 3, 2024 payment was not applied to the June rent. D. Whitfield stated that the landlord's policy is to apply payments to the oldest outstanding balance, which he claims was the May rent. Atty. Okafor argued that the payment confirmation from the rental assistance program explicitly states the payment is for the June rent period. The judge took the matter under advisement and will issue a written ruling within 30 days. Ms. Santos was relieved and thanked us. – R. Chen

**9/20/2024** – Received a voicemail from Ms. Santos asking if there is any update. I returned her call and told her that the judge will issue a written ruling within 30 days and that we will notify her as soon as we receive it. She said she understands and thanked me. – R. Chen

**9/24/2024** – Received a copy of the court's docket entry confirming the hearing on 9/17/2024 and that the matter is under advisement. Filed a copy in the case file. – R. Chen

**9/30/2024** – No update from the court. I called the clerk's office to check on the status of the ruling. The clerk said the judge is still reviewing the case and no ruling has been issued yet. I noted this in the file. – R. Chen

**10/3/2024** – Received an email from D. Whitfield stating that the landlord is willing to settle the case. The landlord would agree to dismiss the eviction action if Ms. Santos agrees to pay the June 2024 rent in full, and the landlord would apply the rental assistance payment to the May rent as originally done. I forwarded this to Atty. Okafor for review. – R. Chen

**10/4/2024** – Atty. Okafor discussed the settlement offer with Ms. Santos. She said she cannot afford to pay the June rent in full right now, but she could pay a portion. Atty. Okafor instructed me to draft a counteroffer proposing that Ms. Santos pay $500 toward the June rent and that the landlord dismiss the eviction action. I drafted the counteroffer and sent it to D. Whitfield. – R. Chen

Client called. He reported that on 05/19, he received a notice from the
landlord stating his lease would not be renewed at the end of the current
term (lease expires 07/31/2024). Notice states reason: "non-renewal, no
cause." Client is concerned this is retaliation for the demand letter.
Advise client to keep the notice. We will review the lease terms and Oregon
law regarding non-renewal notice requirements. ORS 90.427 requires 90 days'

Client has been in the unit since 06/2021. The notice is dated 05/19/2024,

0453 8722 03.

documents.title: Case File 2024-2210 – Closed
documents.content:
Case File 2024-2210 – Closed

06/10/2024 – K. Okafor.
Client called. He received a voicemail from Alder Property Group on 06/07
stating they would “review the matter” but no written response. Client is
anxious. Explained that the 90-day notice period runs from the date the
tenant is served, and that even if the landlord withdraws the notice, we
should get it in writing. Client agreed to wait until 06/21 before
escalating.

Also, client reported the hallway drip has started staining the carpet.
Advised him to document with photos and to keep all receipts for any
cleaning supplies. Referred him to the City of Portland rental housing
inspections program if the landlord does not address the leak within 14
days. Client said he would call them himself if needed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

06/17/2024 – R. Castellanos.
Received letter from Alder Property Group, LLC, dated 06/12/2024. They
withdraw the non-renewal notice. They state the lease will be renewed on a
month-to-month basis after 07/31/2024, per the original lease terms. They
do not admit any defect in the original notice. They also state they will
send a maintenance contractor to inspect the ceiling leak on 06/20/2024
between 1:00 PM and 4:00 PM.

Reviewed lease. Section 3 of the lease states that after the initial term,
the tenancy converts to month-to-month unless either party gives written
notice of non-renewal at least 90 days prior to the end of the term. The
landlord’s position is consistent with the lease. The withdrawal of the
non-renewal notice resolves the retaliation issue for now, but we should
monitor for any further adverse action within six months.

Sent copy of the letter to client via email and regular mail. Advised him
to allow the contractor access but to document the condition of the ceiling
and hallway before and after the inspection.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

06/20/2024 – K. Okafor.
Client called at 3:10 PM. Contractor (name: “Mike” from Alder’s vendor,
Pacific Crest Maintenance) arrived at 1:30 PM and left at 2:45 PM. Client
says Mike looked at the living room ceiling, took photos, and said he would
“report back.” Mike did not do any repair work. Client asked if he should
expect a follow-up. I told him to wait a week and then call the landlord’s
office to ask for a written repair timeline.

Client also mentioned that he received a text from the landlord’s office
on 06/19 asking if he would be interested in signing a new one-year lease
at a rent increase of $75/month. Client is worried this is retaliation
after the withdrawal of the non-renewal notice. I told him not to respond
to the text until we review it. He will forward the text to me.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

06/24/2024 – R. Castellanos.
Reviewed the text message forwarded by client. Sent 06/19/2024 from a
number registered to Alder Property Group. The text offers a one-year
renewal at $1,475/month (current rent is $1,400/month). The offer is not
in writing and does not state an expiration date.

Per ORS 90.385, a landlord may not retaliate by increasing rent within 180
days of a tenant complaint. The demand letter regarding the mold was sent
in April 2024, which is within the 180-day window. The non-renewal notice
was issued 05/19/2024, also within the window. This rent increase offer,
coming after the withdrawal of the non-renewal, could be viewed as
retaliatory. However, proving retaliation for a rent increase is harder
than for a non-renewal because the landlord can claim market adjustment.
